target_customer: Large consumer packaged goods brands and Fortune 500 operations teams (at YC time); later skilled-trades robotics (current YC page)
problem: Companies pay management consultants for point-in-time analysis of pricing, marketing spend and supply chain. Well Principled aimed to run that analysis continuously as software.
business_model: Enterprise software and AI applications for business decisions (at founding); current positioning is a brain-inspired AI architecture for autonomous robots
product_category: Enterprise AI decision software, later neuroscience-inspired AI

founders.name: Ryan Richt
prior_employers: WashU St. Louis Genome Sequencing Center
Cofactor Genomics (co-founder, CEO for two years)
education: Washington University in St. Louis, BA 2008 and MBA 2008 (Olin)

founders.name: Joseph Wingbermuehle
prior_employers: FPGA high-frequency trading and ML network security startups (per YC page)
education: Washington University in St. Louis, PhD Engineering 2015 (Olin article); YC page says BS Applied Math and PhD Computer Science
founders.background_notes: Called cofounder by the Olin article.

founders.name: Christopher Shafer
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page only; the Olin article does not name him.

competitors.name: Management consulting firms
competitors.what: Human consultants doing single point-in-time analysis of pricing, supply chain and marketing spend
competitors.traction_then: Incumbent spending category; the CEO said he targeted high-paying white-collar consulting jobs

technical_complexity.rationale: Combined operations research literature with machine learning to automate business decisions, run on live company data. The later robotics brain architecture is research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Academic advisory board and integration with client data could be sticky, but the offering overlapped with consultancies and demand planning software.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or acquiring the company.

market_need_then: Fortune 500 companies were piloting early versions in 2019, and consultants charged heavily for periodic analyses. No revenue figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Uses wellprincipled.com, an exact match of the name.

identity.voice_and_tone: Philosophical, long form, mission driven (website and YC page)

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself. The company has described very different products under the same name (business AI, BODYSIM fitness app, robot AI).

pivots.from: AI virtual business consultants for consumer brands (2019)
pivots.to: Brain-inspired AI architecture for autonomous robots and skilled trades, plus a BODYSIM fitness product on the YC page
pivots.why: No source states the reason or date.

outcome_analysis: Well Principled raised a $1M pre-seed and a $1.6M seed with Global Founders Capital by 2019-08, selling AI decision software to Fortune 500 pilots. It is still active with a small team but its public positioning has changed to a robotics AI architecture, so the original market was apparently not the lasting one. No later rounds, revenue or exit were found, so the outcome is unresolved.
notes: Aggregators disagree on totals: CB Insights says $2.95M with a loan as latest round, another lists $2.6M; the Olin article's $2.6M (pre-seed plus seed) is used. The pre-seed date is not stated. CB Insights lists a loan, which is unverified and not recorded. The company's role as 'neural engine for autonomous robots' appears on YC and the website; whether the business pivoted fully is unclear. Founder Christopher Shafer appears only on the YC page.
